rationale: A TD is by definition a member of the Dail; the institution must exist for the reader before its members do.
TDs are returned by constituencies; helpful context but a reader can grasp what a TD is without it.
Seat magnitude counts TDs per constituency; meaningless without knowing what a TD is.
Magnitude is a property of a constituency.
Redistricting is the redrawing of constituency boundaries; there is nothing to redraw without the concept of a constituency.
The paper states redistricting is a necessary consequence of PR: as population shifts, boundaries must move to keep representation even (S1).
Reviews are triggered by and computed from the latest census; the reader must know what the census provides to see why reviews happen when they do.
A review is the institutionalised Irish form of redistricting.
Reviews are now conducted by the Commission, but the review concept predates it (Constituency Commissions), so this is context rather than a blocker.
The Commission is graspable as the independent elections body without redistricting; its boundary role is carried through boundary_review (downgraded per AUDIT.md finding 10).
The Commission reviews Dail constituencies specifically.
PR-STV is a mechanism for achieving PR; the goal must precede the mechanism.
STV counts happen within multi-member constituencies; the reader needs the container to understand the count.
The quota is a component of the STV count.
The quota is one moving part of the STV counting method.
Transfers only exist inside an STV count.
Surplus transfers are defined relative to the quota; without the quota, surpluses make no sense.
Transfers are the mechanism that makes STV proportional in practice.
Article 16.2 fixes member numbers and member-to-population ratios; the reader must know what a member (TD) is.
Article 16.2.3 is a requirement on the ratio in each constituency.
The ratio is anchored to the last preceding census; useful context, but the equal-ratio idea is graspable without it.
The terms of reference are conditions on constituencies.
Item (3) requires county boundaries to be preserved as far as practicable; the reader needs counties to parse the rule list.
Item (2) is the 3-5 seat rule; the rule list cannot be read without the magnitude concept.
The statutory terms sit on top of the constitutional provisions; knowing the constitutional floor clarifies what the statute adds.
Gerrymandering is the abuse of the boundary-drawing power; the power must be understood before its abuse.
EDs matter here as the building blocks constituencies are assembled from; the bare fact of 3,440 small areas is graspable alone.
The Map is defined as the collection of building blocks, which in Ireland are the EDs.
The Map abstraction only makes sense as the raw material from which constituencies are formed.
The adjacency graph is a graph; nodes and edges must be understood first.
The nodes of the adjacency graph are EDs.
The split EDs are exceptions to the land-connected edge definition; the reader must know the graph to appreciate the exception.
A configuration is an assignment of every ED to a constituency.
The labels being assigned are constituencies.
A configuration is one way of carving the Map; the Map framing sharpens but is not strictly required.
The rule set is the codified criteria governing redistricting; without the activity there is nothing for rules to govern.
The Irish terms of reference are the worked example of a rule set; the abstract idea is graspable without them.
The constitutional provisions are the strictest layer of the Irish rule set.
A Boundaries object is a configuration that passes the rules; the underlying object must exist first.
Validity is defined relative to the rule set.
The solution space is the set of all configurations; you cannot count what you cannot define.
The numerator of the National Ratio is the census population.
The denominator is the number of Dail seats (TDs).
The paper introduces the National Ratio explicitly in line with Article 16.2.3 (S2.2).
SER is defined as population divided by the National Ratio (Eq. 2).
SER is computed for a proposed constituency's population.
SER quantifies the seats a population deserves, turning the PR ideal into a measurable quantity.
Variance is defined directly in terms of SER (Eq. 6).
Variance compares SER to the assigned integer seat count; the reader must know seats come in whole numbers 3-5.
Variance from the national average operationalises Article 16.2.3's same-ratio-throughout-the-country requirement.
The ±5 percent convention is a threshold on variance.
The convention comes from review-report practice 1980-2023; the historical context explains its status as convention rather than law.
The alternative definition is a modification of the standard one; the contrast is the content.
Same numerator, different denominator: v_new divides by deserved seats so over- and under-representation at the threshold carry equal misrepresentation per person (App C).
Contiguity is a property of a constituency's territory.
The computable definition (one connected component) lives on the graph, but the one-piece idea is graspable without it.
Item (4) of the terms of reference makes contiguity a legal requirement (S1).
Compactness is a property of a constituency's shape.
The paper introduces compactness explicitly to avoid the meandering shapes of manipulated constituencies (S2.4).
The convex hull is one way to measure compactness; the goal precedes the instrument.
One of several interchangeable compactness measures discussed in S2.4.
The metric counts breaches of county boundaries.
The measure is defined on county-boundary edges of the graph (S2.5).
Item (3) makes county preservation a statutory consideration; the metric exists to serve it.
Community boundaries are implemented as designated penalty edges in the graph.
The paper introduces community edges via the same labelled-edge mechanism as county boundary edges (S2.5), though with the opposite penalty trigger (split vs joined).
Continuity compares the proposed configuration against the existing one; both must be understood as configurations.
Continuity is judged between successive reviews; the review cycle is the natural context.
Item (6) requires continuity of existing arrangements to be upheld as far as possible.
The worked example (S2.7, Fig 5) weights county-boundary breaches by the population transferred.
The bump function's x-axis is the SER lying over the boundary; unreadable without SER.
The idea of weighting a breach by people affected is introduced via the continuity function f_C (S2.6 to S2.7).
An objective function acts on configurations; the domain must exist before the function.
The score measures adherence to the rules; without the rule set there is nothing to score.
The objective function is the mathematical operationalisation of the legal rule set (S2).
In this course the Hamiltonian is meaningful only as physics' name for a configuration score to be minimised; the score idea is the genuine comprehension blocker.
The Potts model is defined by its Hamiltonian (Eq. 9); the model cannot be stated without it.
Nearest-neighbour pairs on a lattice are easiest to read as graph edges, but a grid picture suffices.
The ferromagnetic configuration is defined as the minimiser of the Potts Hamiltonian.
The electoral model is an instantiation of the Potts model; the template must precede the instance.
The model's states are exactly the redistricting configurations.
Geographical ED borders translate directly into nearest-neighbour lattice sites (S4.1.1); the graph is the lattice.
The physics bridge: EDs are spins, constituency labels are spin values, ED borders are lattice bonds; grasping the electoral model IS grasping this analogy.
The electoral Potts model is the paper's mathematical formalisation of the redistricting problem.
H_P is a term of the electoral Potts Hamiltonian, defined over its constituencies and populations.
Understanding why H_P takes a minimum over allowed seat counts m requires the seats-deserved idea that SER makes precise.
The set {m_s} = {3,4,5} inside H_P is the seat-magnitude rule.

H_P is built directly on

, the average population per seat - numerically the National Ratio; the paper's 'per constituency' phrasing is a loose carry-over (AUDIT.md finding 1).
H_P penalises exactly the deviation from allowed integer representation that variance measures (Fig 13 marks the 5 percent variance line).
H_C is a term of the electoral Potts Hamiltonian defined over constituency groupings.
H_C counts departures from one-connected-group-per-constituency; the contiguity concept is the content.
H_C = sum |G_q - 1| is the computable form of the contiguity requirement.
H_D is a term of the electoral Potts Hamiltonian defined over neighbouring ED pairs.
H_D is the border-length compactness measure; the compactness goal must precede its encoding.
H_D counts cross-constituency neighbour pairs, the model's definition of (non-)compactness (fn 2).
The physics bridge for a pitfall: H_D alone is minimised by the all-aligned (single-constituency) state, showing what pure compactness pressure does.
The candidate county Hamiltonians are terms of the electoral Potts model.
The three candidates H(1)-H(3) are alternative encodings of the county-breach measure; the measure and its ambiguity must come first.
Each candidate formula operationalises one legal interpretation of a county-boundary violation (S4.1.1, S2.5).
Coupling constants only exist because several objectives must be combined into one function; without the multi-objective problem they are unmotivated.
The missing legal hierarchy is what the constants must supply; knowing the gap makes their role intelligible.
The J_alpha are the numerical translation of the (assumed) hierarchy of rules - the paper's stated first objective (S4.1.1).
The total Hamiltonian is a J-weighted sum; the weights must be understood first.
The sum is unintelligible without at least its principal terms; H_P is the most important of them.
H_C is a summand of the total Hamiltonian.
H_D is a summand of the total Hamiltonian.
County terms may be added in the same manner; optional in the paper's minimal model.
H_P is a component term of H = sum J_alpha H_alpha (Eq. 12).
H_C is a component term of Eq. 12.
H_D is a component term of Eq. 12.
A county term is an optional component of Eq. 12, pending choice among H(1)-H(3).
H_D alone is minimised by one giant constituency while H_P demands Q constituencies at allowed population multiples; verifiable from Eq. 11 though not stated as a tension in the paper.
Temperature only means anything here relative to an energy scale: it calibrates how much energy increase the search will tolerate.
Temperature's role is to control an optimisation's explore/exploit balance.
The Boltzmann weight is a function of the energy H.
The Boltzmann weight is a function of T; the low-T limit is the whole point.
The distribution is over the space of configurations; picturing that space helps but the formula stands without it.
Optimisation is defined as driving a function to an extremum; there must be a function to drive.
The scale of the space explains why optimisation must be clever, but stepwise improvement is graspable without it.
Multi-objective optimisation is optimisation with several competing scores.
The multiple objectives are the multiple rules; the Irish rule set is the concrete instance.
A local minimum is a failure mode of optimisation; the process must precede its pathology.
A move transforms one configuration into another.
Moves are restricted to boundary EDs flipping to graph-neighbouring constituencies; the restriction is defined on the graph.
The move design exists partly to preserve near-contiguity during search (S2.3).
Sampling is motivated by the impossibility of enumeration, though the polling idea stands alone.
Our chains walk on the space of configurations, but the memoryless-walk idea is self-contained.
MCMC is Monte Carlo sampling realised through a Markov chain; both parents are needed.
The chain is the mechanism producing the samples.
MCMC here is a random walk on the state space of configurations (S3.4, S6.2); without the space the walk has nowhere to happen - and the space's size is why sampling is needed at all.
The target distribution in this application is the Boltzmann distribution, but MCMC is definable for any target.
Detailed balance is a condition on a Markov chain's transition probabilities.
Detailed balance is a condition on any Markov chain; MCMC supplies the motivation for caring, not the comprehension (downgraded per AUDIT.md finding 10).
In this application the target lambda is the Boltzmann distribution.
Metropolis-Hastings is a recipe for constructing MCMC transition kernels.
The accept rule is derived precisely so that detailed balance holds (Eqs 30-32); without it the construction is unmotivated magic.
The Metropolis algorithm is the symmetric-proposal special case of Metropolis-Hastings (D.1.1).
The acceptance probability exp(-Delta H/T) is the Boltzmann weight of the energy change.
Metropolis is defined for any energy function (the generic Hamiltonian arrives via the Boltzmann distribution); in the electoral application each step evaluates Delta H of the full weighted sum.

In the practical search the boundary-flip move plays the proposal role, but it is NOT the boxed S4.1.1 proposal (uniform over the other Q-1 constituencies, Eq. 35, symmetric): the restricted move is asymmetric and needs a Metropolis-Hastings correction to preserve detailed balance (AUDIT.md finding 2).
The Gibbs sampler is the always-accept special case of Metropolis-Hastings (D.1.2).
The Gibbs proposal weights all Q options by their Boltzmann factors.
Gibbs is defined for any energy function; in the electoral application each step evaluates Delta H of the full weighted sum for every candidate constituency.
Same target distribution, different economics: Metropolis is cheap per step but rejects proposals; Gibbs never rejects but evaluates all Q options per step.
Annealing IS a schedule on the temperature; nothing to schedule without it.
Annealing is a strategy for global optimisation.
Escaping local extrema is the problem annealing solves (Fig 15); without that problem the slow cooling is pointless ceremony.
The formal definition - sampling from the temperature-dependent equilibrium distribution as T falls - is unintelligible without the Boltzmann picture (promoted per AUDIT.md finding 9).
An ensemble is a sample from the space of valid alternatives; the space is the population being sampled.
The ensemble members are valid boundary configurations under the same rules.
MCMC is the paper's chosen ensemble generator, but the comparison-ensemble idea stands independently.
The hard/soft split is a classification of the terms of reference items (S1).
Context only: the paper's hard/soft split classifies the six terms-of-reference items (S1); the constitutional layer sits above the split (downgraded per AUDIT.md finding 10).
The hierarchy problem concerns ranking among the soft constraints; the reader must first know which ones are soft.
The hierarchy problem is the legal face of the weighting problem in multi-objective optimisation.
One side of the trade-off is the variance measure itself.
The other side is county-boundary preservation.
The trade-off is stated as loosening or tightening the ±5 percent threshold (App C.2); the threshold is the dial being turned.
App C.2: the tighter the variance threshold, the less flexibility to maintain county boundaries; Laois-Offaly proves the conflict is real, not hypothetical.
Population change means keeping boundaries still and keeping representation equal cannot both hold; every report acknowledges balancing continuity against population growth (S3.3.2).

A design tension in the search, not the law: constraining the walk to strictly contiguous maps narrows exploration and risks trapping in local minima, so the paper penalises rather than forbids breaks during search (S2.3).
The paper asserts the magnitude-proportionality link without STV mechanics (S3.7); PR plus seat magnitude carry the dilemma, STV only deepens it (downgraded per AUDIT.md finding 10).
Seat magnitude is the dial the dilemma turns on: more seats, more proportionality, more geographic clustering.
Selection happens among valid Boundaries; the multiplicity of valid answers creates the problem.
Sorting acceptable from unacceptable boundaries encodes one's stance on the hierarchy (S3.2 process A).
The concrete trade-offs are what make selection a genuine decision rather than a lookup.
MCDA is meaningful here as the formal home of the selection problem.
MCDA presupposes options scored on multiple criteria.
MCDA methods make the paper's process B (choosing the recommended boundary) explicit and auditable; the paper describes the step but does not name MCDA.
Pareto optimality is defined with respect to multiple objectives.
The variance/county trade-off is the concrete Irish instance a frontier would display.
The frontier is the standard formal object capturing 'you cannot improve one objective without worsening another'; the paper exhibits the trade-off without the formalism.
MCDA typically operates on (or generates) the non-dominated set.
The parameter space being explored is the space of coupling-constant values.
Comparing results across weight settings is an ensemble-style analysis.
The transparency critique is about what current review reports do and do not disclose; the reader must know the current process to see the gap.
The interpretability claim is precisely that each of the few parameters (the J_alpha) can be individually debated.
Contrast with thousand-parameter black-box optimisers gives the claim its force.
The support is for a specific decision-maker; without the Commission the claim has no subject.
The workload argument (EU, LEA and Dail reviews possibly coinciding) frames why support matters.
What the tool supports is precisely the multi-objective weighing the human must still own.
What is being tested is the rule set; treating rules as adjustable inputs is the conceptual step.
The flagship what-if (allowing 6-seaters, S3.3) is a seat-magnitude question.
Rule experiments run through the same sweep machinery as weight experiments.
Testing resilience against gerrymandering is one of the stated use cases (S1).
The values-in, maps-out claim is about what the rule set encodes; the reader needs the encoding to see where values enter.
The precise claim is that choosing the function (and its weights) is normative while minimising it is mechanical; both halves must be understood.
The missing hierarchy is the clearest example of a normative gap mathematics cannot fill.
Equal representation is the substantive content of legitimacy in this course.
Legitimacy claims here are cashed out in variance: how far each citizen's representation departs from the national norm.
The course's legitimacy argument rests jointly on fair outcomes and a checkable process.
That humans remain accountable for the final map is part of why algorithmic assistance is legitimate rather than threatening.
The unresolved magnitude dilemma tempers any claim that one map is simply 'the fair one'.
Legitimacy requires knowing which choices were value judgements and which were mechanical.
A scrutinisable method is part of what makes algorithm-assisted boundaries defensible to the public.
Monte Carlo estimates averages from random draws; 'i.i.d. draws from a distribution' and the law of large numbers presuppose the distribution-and-sampling idea.
A Markov chain's transition rule is a probability distribution over next states conditioned on the current one; without distributions the memoryless walk cannot be stated.
The Boltzmann weight defines a probability distribution over configurations; assigning maps probabilities is the whole content of Eq. 13.
The concept's defining example f_PR (Eq. 7) is a function of |Variance| and assigned seats; the reader must know variance before the example is readable (AUDIT.md finding 7).
The J/T rescaling degeneracy (S5.1.1) pairs the weights with the search temperature; kept soft - the concept text flags it as a forward reference.
